speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if you can point to the specific spot that hurts the most?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The patient's history of pain in the right thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow, exacerbated by holding an infant and relieved by ice, is highly suggestive of this condition. The family history of rheumatoid arthritis (mother on methotrexate) and the remote fall are less likely to be the primary cause of her current symptoms. I will recommend a clinical test to confirm the diagnosis.
